observations.seen: Black void on desktop; empty untextured box room on mobile. No pool hall, no lamp, no props.
Table is boxy kit-bash: block legs, disc pockets, flat rail strips. Balls are fine spheres. No cue stick at all.
No visible textures. Felt is flat color, rails have no wood grain, balls lack numbers and stripes.
Rails read as orange plastic. Felt has no fiber or sheen. Balls have a decent gloss highlight, which is the only credible material.
Spec highlights exist, but there is no energy-conserving roughness variety and the felt behaves like an unlit or emissive surface.
Arbitrary colored hotspots (cyan, magenta, orange) contradict the "one lamp" fiction. No overhead light pool. Felt is evenly lit.
No readable ball shadows on the felt and no table shadow on the floor, so nothing grounds the objects.
Pure black ambient with no AO in pockets, rail joins, or under balls.
Balls show point-light glints only, with no environment reflection. Rails have no reflection either.
Desktop is mostly in range but the felt blue is oversaturated. The mobile lamp hotspot clips hard to white.
Palette is garish: electric blue felt against orange rails against neon accents. Probably sRGB-correct, but authored without restraint.
Edges and decal lines look acceptable at 1080p. Mobile at small scale shows shimmer-prone sub-pixel balls.
No visible bloom discipline, AO, DOF, vignette, or grading. The rail glows look like light leaks, not deliberate bloom.
Only the aim line and target-circle decals. No impact, pocket, or charge effects.
None visible in any frame.
Physics balls only. No cue animation, and nothing changes between "mid" and "action" except ball positions.
The player avatar in pool is the cue stick, and it is absent, so there is no physical agency in-world.
A single static high 3/4 shot never moves. Mobile camera is far too distant.
The table is off-center against a void with huge dead space top and bottom, and the HUD crowds the right edge.
Without shadows, room, or fog, the table reads as a floating model and scale is ambiguous.
No lamp haze, smoke, dust, or fog.
Ball positions and decals read clearly on desktop. Stripes vs. solids cannot be told apart, which is fatal for "clear your suit." Mobile is close to unreadable.
Clean dark-glass panel and a consistent grid, but it is a dev dashboard: debug backend text, empty "…" placeholders, duplicated status messages.
Legible sans with sensible hierarchy. Generic, with tiny label sizes and no game identity.
No feedback on any action and placeholder text visible. Reads as a prototype, as its own label says.
Tiny table in a dark box, a blown hotspot, and 40% of the screen spent on buttons. Effectively unplayable visually.
A clean programmer-art prototype. Sits below "dated but competent" because the void, missing cue, and missing shadows are basic omissions.
